metadata.description: Demo input for code_demo.ipynb: labelled per-sample rows of ONE dataset (T2 weighted shortest path) plus the small files method.py's assemble() reads, so the notebook can rebuild the artifact folder and run assemble() unchanged.
metadata.selection: seeded random sample (random.Random(20261019)) of T2 rows inside each runs/labelled_*.jsonl file (one arm x condition), spread over prompt paraphrases; no filtering on label or pass/fail
metadata.support_files_note: support_files maps a path inside the artifact folder to its content: parsed JSON for .json, a string for raw-text files (kept byte-exact so the forecast's sha256 still matches). results/*.json are the analyses of the FULL run (4140 programs, both tasks). data/prompts.json keeps only the T2 prompt texts (token ids dropped).

spec.t1: Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal). grid is a list of equal-length strings in which . is a free cell and # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of free cells. A move goes up, down, left or right to a free cell inside the grid. Return a list of (row, col) tuples forming a valid path from start to goal, including both ends; any valid path is accepted. If goal cannot be reached, return an empty list. The grid has at most 30 rows and 30 columns. Use only the Python standard library.
spec.t2: Task: write a Python function solve(n, edges, s, t). The graph is directed with nodes 0..n-1 (n <= 100). edges is a list of (u, v, w) tuples, each an edge from u to v with integer weight 0 <= w <= 100; there may be cycles, self-loops and parallel edges. Return the length of the shortest path from s to t as an int, or -1 if t is unreachable from s. If s == t return 0. Use only the Python standard library.

    graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for u, v, w in edges:
        graph[u].append((v, w))
